rows.grounds: locative of liṅgāyāma (length of the liṅga); fused form written as liṃgāyāme (anusvāra before y).
locative of daśāṃśa (tenth part); compound daśa+aṃśa.
accusative of guṇāṃśa (part measured by guna/threefold part as per context); compound guṇa+aṃśa.
accusative/nominal form of caturaśraka (four-cornered); compound catur+aśraka.

items.question: What proportional measure is prescribed for the four-cornered form in relation to the liṅga’s length?
premises: The liṅga’s length is taken as the reference measure.
A tenth part is specified in that lengthwise reference.
A guna-part is prescribed as the measure of the four-cornered form.
items.inference: In the liṅga’s length, at a tenth part, the four-cornered form is to be taken as a guna-part.
uncertainties: Exact technical value of guṇāṃśa in this āgamic measurement scheme is not specified by the tokens alone.
items.plain_english: In the length of the liṅga, at the tenth part, take the four-cornered form as a guna-part.
